# Why the snorkel vendors slh-dsa

## Provenance

This is a copy of Rostro's vendored `slh-dsa`, which is itself the
crates.io `0.1.0` tarball (sha256
`069c0368c5352eeea0134fa9bfd45feb28c5c5412719b2db81c12c784adb1aef`,
pinned 2026-07-05) with two build-only changes. `VENDOR.md` alongside
this file is Rostro's original note and remains authoritative on the
upstream pin, the parameter-set choice, and the modifications; nothing
in it was edited.

Rostro's two changes, restated because they are the reason this copy
exists rather than a crates.io dependency:

1. `signature` requirement `"2.3.0-pre.4"` → `">=2.0, <3"`. Upstream
   0.1.0 pinned a **pre-release** of the `signature` trait crate. Cargo
   will not unify a pre-release caret requirement with the stable
   `signature 2.x` that `ed25519-dalek` resolves through `ed25519`, so
   stock `slh-dsa 0.1.0` and `ed25519-dalek` cannot coexist in one
   dependency graph. Since a hybrid signature needs *both*, the
   relaxation is mandatory for any consumer of the scheme.
2. Inverted `no_std` gate corrected, plus explicit alloc imports in the
   seven files that needed them.

Neither touches algorithm logic. Behaviour is pinned by the ACVP and
SPHINCS+ reference KATs shipped in `tests/`, which pass unchanged.

## Why a copy instead of depending on Rostro

The snorkel is a separate, self-contained codebase. It builds and ships
without the chain repo present, and someone auditing the resolver
should not need to fetch a second tree to see every byte that verifies
a finality signature.

The reasoning is also Rostro's own, from `VENDOR.md`: *"a
consensus-critical cryptographic primitive we ship is ours to audit,
freeze, and patch — a CVE in it is our issue, not upstream's."* The
snorkel now ships this primitive too, so the same obligation attaches
here.

## Drift protection

The snorkel does **not** reuse Rostro's `rostro-hybrid-sig`. It has its
own verify-only implementation in `crates/snorkel-sync/src/hybrid.rs`,
roughly sixty lines covering the byte layout, the ed25519 domain
preimage, and the SLH-DSA context binding.

Two independent implementations of one wire format can silently
diverge, so `crates/snorkel-sync/vectors/hybrid_finality_v1.txt` holds a
real `(public key, message, signature)` triple **generated by the
chain's own signer**. The test `accepts_a_real_chain_signature` verifies
it here. If Rostro ever changes the domain string, the preimage framing,
the context binding, or the byte layout, that test fails in this repo —
rather than the snorkel quietly rejecting every genuine justification
in production.

Regenerating the vector requires the Rostro tree and a signing key; it
is deliberately a manual, reviewed act, not an automated refresh.

## Updating

Do not track upstream automatically (Dependabot-as-intel, not as a
queue). Re-evaluate when `slh-dsa 0.2.0` is stable and its dependency
generation stops being an all-RC stack. Any update must keep this copy
byte-compatible with the chain's, since a divergence means the snorkel
rejects real signatures.
